chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Amiri from Safwan from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: 'In the Mu'arras (the place where the Prophet's tent was pitched), the Mu'arras of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): When you return to Medina, pass by it, dismount, let down its load, and pray in it, for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did that.'
I said: 'What if it is not the time for prayer?' He said: 'Then establish the call to prayer (Iqamah).' I said: 'My companions will not establish it.' He said: 'Then pray two rak'ahs and proceed.'
And he said: 'The Mu'arras is [specifically] when you return to Medina, not when you set out.'

key_terms.إِقَامَة: The second call to prayer, distinct from Adhan
key_terms.الْمُعَرَّس: The place where the Prophet's tent was pitched in Medina
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended ritual practice when visiting the Prophet's Mu'arras in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the specific timing for visiting the Prophet’s *Mu'arras* (tent site), specifying it is recommended upon returning to Medina rather than at the outset of a journey. The Imam’s instruction to perform dismounting rituals and pray two rak'ahs—even if not in prayer time—highlights the site’s enduring spiritual significance as a place of connection with the Prophet’s legacy. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *ziyarat* (visitation) and replicating the Prophet’s daily habits to maintain a tangible link to his presence.
